R7-C001.title: Evidence retention does blocking fsync I/O under one process-global mutex on the per-core async runtime
R7-C001.evidence: Confirmed as stated, and it had got WORSE: the owner's execution-boundary work added `reserve()`, a SECOND synchronous fsync chain, pre-dispatch. Derivation appended to work/security-audit-2026-08-03/DESIGN-retention-state-machine.md as 'Part 2 — the concurrency and acknowledgement model' before any code was written, because `spawn_blocking` keeps the process-global mutex (it only moves the queue of blocked threads) and a fire-and-forget channel deletes the acknowledgement Part 1 exists to preserve.
R7-C001.action: transparency.rs: the store is owned outright by ONE dedicated OS thread (`write_loop`, thread `mcp-re-retention`) — not a runtime worker, not a blocking-pool thread — so there is no mutex on the request path and no mutex at all. `reserve`/`complete`/`retain` are async: each serializes its record (CPU only), hands a `WriteJob` carrying a `oneshot::Sender` to the writer, and AWAITS the acknowledgement. The writer sends ONLY after the durability boundary for that job is crossed, never on enqueue, so it is not fire-and-forget: the reserve ack is a precondition of dispatch and the complete ack a precondition of the success result. Overload is a process-global semaphore of K=1024 reservations taken with `try_acquire` in `reserve` — pre-dispatch, retry-safe 503 `evidence_retention_unavailable`, backend untouched — and NEVER a post-execution drop; the channel is sized 2K so `complete` can never find it full. The directory barrier is group-committed (one `fsync(D)` per batch of up to 64 renames, derived from the fact that a directory fsync has no per-entry granularity); the per-object `sync_all` before its own rename stays, and is NOT downgraded to `sync_data` because the 0600 mode is not in fdatasync's obligation. Tests (transparency.rs): `the_fsync_does_not_run_on_the_runtime_worker` (on a `new_current_thread` runtime a spawned task only runs while the retaining task is suspended at an await — an inline write never yields, so the flag stays false without the fix), `an_acknowledged_write_is_already_at_its_final_name`, `a_full_reservation_queue_is_refused_at_reserve_and_the_slot_returns`, `completion_is_never_refused_for_capacity`, `a_reservation_marker_is_durable_before_dispatch_and_cleared_after`.

R7-C009.title: Round-6 per-actor replay budget lives only in a store `app.rs` unconditionally refuses to serve with
R7-C009.evidence: Verified: the round-6 per-actor budget (per_actor_budget/under_pressure) was implemented ONLY inside InMemoryAsyncAtomicReplayStore::insert_locked, a store that declares SingleProcessReference (async_replay.rs:103-105) and that app.rs:619 refuses to start with; async_redis_store.rs and async_etcd_store.rs both discarded insert.actor. Correct arithmetic, unreachable enforcement.
R7-C009.action: Enforcement moved ABOVE the backend seam: new RetentionLedger inside AsyncReplayTier (mcp-re-proxy/src/async_replay.rs) charges every admitted nonce to key.principal before the store is touched, commits the charge on Fresh with the skew-folded retain_until, releases it on Replay/error, and prunes by expiry bucket against the verifier's now_unix. The ledger is Arc-shared by every clone of the tier, so one replica has one account. per_actor_budget is unchanged arithmetic except that it now splits the SPENDABLE capacity (ceiling minus reserve) instead of the full ceiling, so no number of actors can spend the reserve. The reservation is an RAII Charge guard rather than a hand-settled counter, because the serving path awaits the handler inside a hyper service: a peer that closes its connection drops the future mid-insert, and a charge settled only on the return paths would leak on exactly that one - permanently, so an actor cancelling in flight could walk the tier to its ceiling and fail every signer closed. Tests (async_replay.rs): the_tier_budgets_a_durable_backend_that_budgets_nothing_itself (drives a Durable store that budgets nothing; greedy actor stops at 8 of a 10-entry ceiling, quiet actor still admitted, over-budget refusal is McpReError::ReplayCacheUnavailable AND does not dispatch to the backend at all - dispatch counter asserted), a_replay_hands_the_charge_back, the_tier_releases_charges_once_their_retention_expires, no_number_of_actors_can_spend_the_reserve, the_budget_reserves_headroom_and_splits_evenly, an_abandoned_insert_does_not_leak_its_charge (50 abandoned inserts against a never-answering Durable store leave zero charges and the tier still serving). SIZING NOTE FOR THE OWNER: the ledger's ceiling is the pre-existing ASYNC_MAX_ENTRIES (1,000,000) and it now applies to the Redis and etcd deployments too, where before there was no per-replica ceiling at all. Since an entry is held for its whole retain_until, one principal's sustained per-replica rate is capped at roughly (max_entries - reserve) / retention_window - about 2,700 rps at a 300s window, about 200 rps at the 3900s worst case. That is above the SLO anchor (~4900 rps measured over a short run, ~150k entries) but it is a real production ceiling that did not exist before, so the constant should be sized deliberately against the §7 SLO rather than inherited.

R7-C020.title: Every unauthenticated TLS ClientHello forces one KMS/HSM sign on the delegated-TLS path
R7-C020.evidence: Confirmed: `DelegatedEd25519Signer::sign` is the single choke point for the server's TLS CertificateVerify on the delegated custody paths, TLS 1.3 signs it before the client's Certificate is seen, and `refuse_session_resumption` makes every connection a full handshake — so cheap inbound TCP converted 1:1 into paid, quota-limited KMS Sign calls against the same account the cold-path delegated-key issuer uses.
R7-C020.action: delegated_tls.rs: `TlsHandshakeSignBudget`, a token bucket (`DEFAULT_TLS_SIGN_RATE_PER_SEC` 100/s sustained, `DEFAULT_TLS_SIGN_BURST` 200) checked in `Signer::sign` BEFORE the remote signer is touched; exhaustion refuses the handshake with an explicit `rustls::Error`, which is the fail-closed direction (a refused connection costs the peer a retry; an exhausted KMS quota is a fleet-wide outage at the keys' exp). A poisoned lock counts as exhausted. Refusals are counted for the operator posture. The rate is sized against what legitimate traffic needs given no resumption and `max_connection_age` 300s. Tests: `handshake_signature_budget_bounds_remote_signer_invocations` (counts backend invocations, not just the error), `handshake_signature_budget_refills_over_time`.

R7-C022.title: Unauthenticated peer forces one blocking KMS/PKCS#11 handshake signature per TCP connection, unbounded
R7-C022.evidence: Confirmed: nothing between the accept loop and `sign_tls_ed25519` bounded either the RATE or the CONCURRENCY of handshake signatures; `DELEGATED_TLS_WORKERS_PER_CORE = 4` is a pool, and the module's own doc says a pool 'only widens the window before the pool is exhausted'. TLS 1.3 signs CertificateVerify before the client's Certificate is seen, so no credential is needed to drive it.
R7-C022.action: Two bounds, one per axis. RATE: the `TlsHandshakeSignBudget` token bucket in delegated_tls.rs (see R7-C020/C021). CONCURRENCY: async_serve.rs adds a per-core handshake admission semaphore of `DELEGATED_TLS_HANDSHAKES_PER_CORE = 2`, installed ONLY where a handshake can block (`options.tls_signing_may_block`; on the exported-key path the signature is in-memory and bounding it would cost throughput for nothing). Held strictly below the worker pool, so a core under handshake flood always retains workers for its accept loop, its established connections and its in-flight requests. Waiting for the permit is safe in a way the signature is not — that await YIELDS, so `request_deadline` really does preempt it, and a connection that cannot get in before the deadline is dropped rather than queued; the permit is released once the handshake completes, not at the end of the connection, because an established connection costs no further device signatures. Test: `async_serve::admission_bound_tests::the_handshake_bound_leaves_workers_for_the_rest_of_the_core` pins the strictly-below-the-pool invariant, which is the thing a future edit would silently undo.

R7-C080.title: RFC 9162 fold still admits restated (leaf_index, tree_size) — the round-6 binding claim is false

I re-derived the fold by hand: for (leaf_index=1, tree_size=2) with one sibling the walk gives fnode=1 (odd) -> r=H(sib,r), fnode=0, snode=0, terminal check passes; for (2,3) fnode=2==snode=2 -> same branch, the promote-loop drives fnode/snode to 1/1 then 0/0, terminal check passes, SAME root. The whole (2^k, 2^k+1) family behaves identically. This is not a bug in the fold: RFC 9942's RFC9162_SHA256 receipt payload is the bare Merkle Tree Hash, which unlike an RFC 9162 signed tree head never covers `tree_size`, and a right-edge leaf is promoted past every level - so the tree hash of leaf 2^k of a 2^k+1-leaf log IS the same computation as leaf 1 of a 2-leaf log. No fold can separate them. Confirmed no consumer builds a security decision on the accessors: the only readers workspace-wide are assertions in scitt.rs, mcp-re-conformance/tests/scitt_interop_test.rs:157-158 and scitt_vectors_test.rs:466-467.

(2) `Receipt::tree_size` / `Receipt::leaf_index` - both the struct fields and the public accessors - documented as UNAUTHENTICATED transport hints that no ordering, anchoring, freshness or log-maturity reasoning may rest on. (3) The regression test was pinning only the positions that already failed; renamed to `restating_the_log_position_at_a_different_path_length_does_not_verify` and added `a_right_edge_restatement_is_indistinguishable_and_still_verifies`, which asserts every (2^k, 2^k+1) for k in 1..8 verifies AND folds to the honest 2-leaf root, so the residual is pinned rather than latent. OWNER DECISION: binding the log position needs the transparency service to SIGN the tree size - an RFC 9162 STH profile beyond RFC 9942's RFC9162_SHA256 - which changes receipt wire bytes and the frozen mcp-re-conformance/tests/vectors/scitt/ corpus. Alternative: remove the accessors.
R7-C080.owner_correction: Scope was understated. The (2^k, 2^k+1) family named in `action` is one class among many, so refusing ambiguous positions is not an available defence. Recorded as an exhaustive finite measurement, not an algebraic characterisation. Separately measured: no class contains two members sharing a tree_size. That is NOT the chosen fix — it is a property of the current verification algorithm rather than of the evidence. RULING: bind the tuple explicitly in a versioned, domain-separated protected-header commitment, coordinated with C082 and C114 in ONE corpus revision with a visible profile transition. See HANDOFF.md.

R7-C087.title: Trust-epoch read timeout exceeds the default rotation overlap window
R7-C087.evidence: Verified: TRUST_EPOCH_TIMEOUT was 30s per socket operation, read_epoch can spend that on the connect, the GET, the reconnect and the retried GET (four operations, up to 120s), and app.rs calls current_label() synchronously in the rotation loop at exp - overlap with a default overlap of 60s (cli.rs). One half-open connection consumed the whole minting window and took response signing down fleet-wide at the current key's exp.
R7-C087.action: The budget is now expressed as a property of the whole READ rather than of one socket op: TRUST_EPOCH_READ_BUDGET = 8s, TRUST_EPOCH_OPS_PER_READ = 4, and TRUST_EPOCH_TIMEOUT is derived as the quotient (2s), so a complete read - including the reconnect and retry - fits in 8s and leaves the great majority of the 60s overlap for the mint it precedes. Test: one_epoch_read_cannot_consume_the_rotation_overlap asserts TRUST_EPOCH_TIMEOUT * TRUST_EPOCH_OPS_PER_READ <= TRUST_EPOCH_READ_BUDGET and TRUST_EPOCH_READ_BUDGET * 2 <= the 60s default overlap, so re-raising the timeout without re-deriving the budget fails the build (feature redis_replay).

R7-C090.title: Trust-epoch poller is unsupervised and its health flag latches true
R7-C090.evidence: Verified: spawn_trust_epoch_poller did a bare thread::spawn with the JoinHandle dropped, no catch_unwind and no liveness record, while is_healthy() read a latch only poll_once writes - so a dead poller left the replica reporting healthy and silently degraded Tier-3 revocation from one poll interval to the trust-cache TTL. A poisoned pending/last_seen mutex additionally dropped the FlushAll permanently without touching healthy.
R7-C090.action: Three changes in trust_epoch.rs. (1) Liveness: the source records last_poll on every poll_once and spawn_trust_epoch_poller installs a bound of (tolerated missed rounds + one read) via require_polling_within; is_healthy() is now `polled_recently() && healthy`, so silence past the bound is unhealthy on its own and a source with a poller that never produced a first read is not healthy. A source nobody spawned a poller over keeps no bound. (2) Supervision: the poll loop runs inside catch_unwind and an unwinding thread calls report_poller_death, which flips healthy false and warns on stderr. (3) Poison: a recover() helper takes the guard back on a poisoned mutex, so a revocation is no longer dropped on the floor; poll_once also pushes the FlushAll BEFORE advancing the baseline, so the flush cannot be lost by advancing without queueing. Tests: a_source_that_stops_being_polled_stops_reporting_healthy, a_poller_that_never_ran_is_not_healthy, a_directly_driven_source_is_not_subject_to_the_liveness_bound, a_poisoned_queue_still_delivers_the_flush, plus the pre-existing read_error_marks_unhealthy_and_emits_nothing and recovery_after_outage_catches_an_epoch_that_advanced_during_it.

R7-C091.title: MRTR cross-replica continuation silently absent on the etcd/linearizable fleet, with no startup line
R7-C091.evidence: Confirmed at app.rs: the continuation store was wired only when `config.replay_redis_url` AND the Redis-only `replay_control_rt` both existed, with no `else`. On `--replay-durability-tier linearizable` both are absent, so `continuation_store: None` and every MRTR answer leg fails closed forever while the proxy still RETURNS `input_required` replies it cannot honour — and nothing said so, unlike the retention and audit seams which both print an OFF line.
R7-C091.action: Two changes. (1) The runtime coupling is gone: the store now takes a control runtime built on demand (`control_runtime`), so it depends only on `--replay-redis-url`. (2) An explicit OFF posture line (`CONTINUATION_STORE_OFF`) is printed in the `else`, and also in a build without `redis_replay`, naming exactly what is lost: 'multi-round-trip flows are SINGLE-REPLICA only. A client that receives an `input_required` reply from one replica and answers on another is refused (mcp-re.continuation_binding_failed).' NOT closed as an etcd-backed continuation store: none exists, and inventing one to close a posture gap would be building the wrong thing — the honest OFF line is the fix the finding asks for (its stated impact is undiagnosability, not the fail-closed itself).

R7-C092.title: --admission cannot be deployed on the linearizable replay tier; refusal blames a flag the operator supplied
R7-C092.evidence: Confirmed at app.rs: `--admission` required `(admission_redis_url, replay_control_rt)`, and `replay_control_rt` was `Some` only inside the Redis replay branch (the etcd branch and the memory branch both set it to None). So `--admission required` + `--replay-durability-tier linearizable` aborted at startup with '--admission requires --admission-redis-url and the replay control runtime' even when the operator HAD supplied `--admission-redis-url` — misattributing the cause to a flag they had passed, whose natural resolution is to turn admission off.
R7-C092.action: The admission source is an independent endpoint and is now wired as one: `let Some(url) = config.admission_redis_url.as_ref() else { return Err("--admission requires --admission-redis-url") }` followed by `control_runtime(&mut control_rt)?`, which builds the shared process-lifetime control runtime on demand. `replay_control_rt` is renamed `control_rt` and is now created by whichever seam needs it first (replay reconnect task, admission source, continuation store), so no seam is gated on another having created it. Admission control is therefore deployable on every replay tier, and the error text names only the flag that is actually missing.

R7-C093.title: Admission degraded window is bounded by assertion age, not by authority-outage duration
R7-C093.evidence: Confirmed: `admission_gate` mapped every source error to `authoritative = None` and kept no record of when the source was last reachable, so `check_admission`'s unreachable branch tested only `now - claims.iat > P + skew`. Since the revocation channel IS the store, during a store outage the issuer never learns of a revocation and keeps minting assertions with a current `iat` — so a caller that kept fetching them was served for the whole outage.
R7-C093.action: http_profile_serve.rs: `AdmissionEnforcer` gains `last_authoritative_read: AtomicI64` (i64::MIN until the first successful read — a replica that never reached the authority has no last-known state, so startup is not a confirmation). `record_authoritative_read` is called on BOTH Ok(Some) and Ok(None), because a definitive negative means the authority answered, which is what P measures; it uses `fetch_max` so an out-of-order read cannot rewind the window. `degraded_window_exhausted(now)` decides whether the §5.2 degraded fork may be entered at all, BEFORE `check_admission` sees the assertion. Tests: unit `http_profile_serve::admission_window_tests` (4: never-read, closes at P+skew exactly, no rewind, no window without the opt-in) and e2e tests/admission_currency_serving_test.rs `an_unreachable_authority_serves_within_p_and_fails_closed_past_it` — REWRITTEN, since the old one drove the window with the assertion's iat, i.e. asserted the defect: every assertion in it is now fresh and only the outage ages — plus a new `a_replica_that_never_reached_the_authority_does_not_enter_degraded_mode`. NOT closed: `VerifiedAdmission::degraded` is still discarded, so a degraded serve is indistinguishable from a live-confirmed one in audit. That is a separate finding's ground (the ADR-MCPS-035 success-event allowlist is frozen and adding a third success event needs an ADR); it is named in the code at the discard site.

R7-C095.title: The manifest rollback floor can be raised without bound by anyone who can write the floor directory
R7-C095.evidence: TRUE as a mechanism and NOT fixable inside the module. mcp-re-client-proxy/src/manifest_floor.rs:read_floor takes max() over marker names with no ceiling, and min_version() is max(directory, bootstrap), so one file named 18446744073709551615 pins the floor at u64::MAX and mcp-re-client-core/src/trust_manifest.rs:298-303 then rejects every future manifest as Stale (including a break-glass revocation). The floor is reached on the serving path: mcp-re-client/src/anchors.rs:104-112 constructs FileManifestFloor::with_bootstrap for FloorConfig::Durable and AnchorLoader::load feeds it to load_signed_manifest_with_floor.
R7-C095.action: No code change. Every in-module bound is either bypassable (a fixed ceiling is a number the same directory-writer stays under) or harmful (an operator ceiling clamps a LEGITIMATE floor down and re-opens the rollback window). The module doc now states the boundary explicitly (manifest_floor.rs:45-56): the floor directory must be permissioned no more widely than the trust store itself; the bootstrap bounds what a directory-writer can take away, not what it can add. Owner ruling wanted on whether that deployment control is accepted as the answer, or whether the floor should move to authenticated storage.
R7-C095.owner_correction: The `action` field's rejection of an operator ceiling is WRONG as stated. It argues a ceiling 'clamps a LEGITIMATE floor down and re-opens the rollback window' — that describes a defective ceiling, not a property of ceilings. Correct behaviour: stored_floor <= trusted_ceiling -> continue normal validation; stored_floor > trusted_ceiling -> FAIL-STOP, inconsistent trusted state. NEVER effective_floor = min(stored_floor, trusted_ceiling). The ceiling must come from a trust domain the floor-directory writer cannot modify or it adds no security. This does not close the finding — it cannot preserve availability after a malicious fast-forward, only fail safely — but it is a real local gain. RULING: security-critical floor state must not be authoritative state writable by the actor it constrains; close as superseded by a trusted-floor-store issue once that issue carries enforceable acceptance criteria. See work/security-audit-2026-08-03/HANDOFF.md.
R7-C095.resolution: FAIL-STOP CEILING LANDED; the finding itself is superseded, not closed. `FileManifestFloor::with_bounds(path, bootstrap, ceiling)` plus config `floor.ceiling_version`. stored_floor <= ceiling -> normal; stored_floor > ceiling -> TrustManifestError::FloorAboveCeiling. NEVER min(). Also refused at `record()` before it can brick the floor, and at construction when bootstrap > ceiling. Test `the_ceiling_never_clamps_the_floor_downward` is the negative control. This buys DETECTION, not availability: a malicious fast-forward still stops the client, but loudly and at a named error instead of silently withdrawing every anchor at manifest expiry. RULING STANDS: security-critical floor state must not be authoritative state writable by the actor it constrains; close as superseded by a trusted-floor-store issue carrying the acceptance criteria in HANDOFF.md.

R7-C139.title: Content-Digest hashes the full 16 MiB body before any signature or keyid work (CPU amplification)
R7-C139.evidence: Real, and the finding's own caveat is the operative one. Confirmed the ordering at verify.rs:807-808 (`required_header("content-digest")` then `verify_content_digest_sha256(digest_header, &request.body)`) with the signature untouched until ~verify.rs:830, and the same shape at verify.rs:1000, 1227, 1379, 1518 and bodyless.rs:670. The signature base needs only the Content-Digest HEADER value, so the ordering is not forced. Availability only, no bypass.
R7-C139.action:
RULED, NOT FIXED - accepted by design; the ordering stands and no policy knob is added. Both candidate fixes are wrong, and the finding's severity framing does not survive measurement.

(a) Reordering (signature first, digest after) is permanently rejected: it puts the trust store on the path of digest-mismatched traffic, reversing the deliberate v0.11 grill C.1 choice, and it changes which wire code fires for a message that is BOTH digest-mismatched and signature-invalid - i.e. it moves frozen conformance vectors.

(b) A body ceiling on VerifierPolicy is rejected, and for a stronger reason than the ownership one first given. Every path into verify_request already passes a read-time ceiling that fails closed BEFORE the body is allocated: ServerLimits::max_body_bytes (16 MiB default, enforced in async_serve.rs collect_body against a per-core byte budget and an aggregate read deadline, so slow-loris on a trickled body is covered too) on the serving path, and ClientLimits::max_response_bytes (16 MiB, mcp-re-transport) on the client. A ceiling re-checked inside verify_request would fire only AFTER that allocation, so it narrows nothing the existing bound does not already refuse, and it hands a deployment two ceilings that can silently disagree.

MEASUREMENT (arm64, OpenSSL 3.x, `openssl speed`, 2026-08-05): SHA-256 2.63 GB/s; AES-256-GCM 6.81 GB/s; Ed25519 verify 18435/s = 54.2 us. For a max-size 16 MiB body: digest ~6.4 ms, the AES-GCM decrypt the server already paid unconditionally ~2.5 ms, signature check 0.054 ms. The finding's 'amplification' is digest/signature ~= 118x - a ratio against the CHEAPEST step, not against the unavoidable per-request cost. Against that cost it is ~2.6x. And to buy 6.4 ms of server SHA-256 the sender must place 16 MiB on the wire, which occupies ~134 ms of a 1 Gbps link: ~0.05 ms of server CPU per ms of attacker link time. It DE-amplifies by roughly 20x. Concurrency is separately bounded at max_in_flight_requests = 256 per core.

R7-C145.title: Shipped audit sink does a synchronous unbounded stderr write per decision, drivable unauthenticated
R7-C145.evidence: Confirmed: `StderrAuditSink::record` was a bare `eprintln!` inline on the request path, reached from `rejection` on EVERY preflight failure — before any signature verifies, so an unauthenticated peer set its rate — violating the trait's own 'MUST NOT block the request path' contract.
R7-C145.action: audit_sink.rs: the line is formatted on the request path and then HANDED OFF to a dedicated `mcp-re-audit` thread that owns stderr, over a bounded `sync_channel` (`STDERR_AUDIT_QUEUE_DEPTH` 4096). `offer` uses `try_send` and counts a full queue as a DROP rather than waiting — which is the same intent from the other side, since a sink must never fail or delay a request — and the drop count is reported on the channel itself so a gap in the record is visible as a gap rather than inferred from silence. Write errors are swallowed on the writer thread, so a closed stderr can no longer panic a connection task.
